Uganda has started withdrawing its troops deployed in Somalia. Uganda has been a major contributor to the international military campaign against insurgents in Somalia. Uganda was the first country to send troops to Somalia after the African Union launched a military campaign to fight Islamic insurgents in 2007. Since then, Uganda has played a major role by deploying thousands of soldiers in various military campaigns of the African Union. However, in recent months, the future of the international military campaign in Somalia has become uncertain after major financial donors, including the United States, cut aid. A statement issued by the Ugandan army said, “The Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) has immediately started the process of withdrawing its troops deployed there under the bilateral agreement with the Federal Government of Somalia.” The statement mentioned that all Ugandan soldiers in Somalia will be gradually withdrawn by the end of 2027. This includes soldiers deployed under the ‘African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia’ (AUSOM). Despite the ongoing international military campaign, the Al-Shabaab group, affiliated with Al-Qaeda, still controls large parts of the central regions of Somalia. Four thousand five hundred to six thousand Ugandan soldiers were deployed in Somalia under the recent African Union mission. Similarly, an additional two thousand to two thousand five hundred soldiers were deployed there under a bilateral agreement. America has withdrawn financial aid to the United Nations’ crucial logistics and supply mission. The military coalition has been dependent on this mission. Washington has expressed dissatisfaction, citing insufficient progress in the fight against Al-Shabaab and the inability of the Somali government to establish national unity and advance political reforms. The Ugandan army stated that with the decision to withdraw troops, its 20-year-long support campaign to establish peace and stability in Somalia will end. The army said this move will enable the Somali armed forces to take full responsibility for the country's security. Disclaimer This specific news has been automatically translated by AI. somalia.content: National Ownership or Premature Abandonment in Somalia’s Dangerous New Phase – HORN REVIEW Home About Us Team Research and Analysis Horn Geopolitics Global Politics Ethiopia and the World Publications News Reports and Articles Horn Review Journal Articles Horn Review Magazine Report Amharic Publications Amharic News Reports and Articles Amharic Research and Analysis Amharic Ethiopia and the World Amharic Global Politics Amharic Horn Geopolitics Amharic Horn Review Journal Articles Amharic horn review magazine Amharic Report News and Events Contact Us Search Home About Us Team Research and Analysis Horn Geopolitics Global Politics Ethiopia and the World Publications News Reports and Articles Horn Review Journal Articles Horn Review Magazine Report Amharic Publications Amharic News Reports and Articles Amharic Research and Analysis Amharic Ethiopia and the World Amharic Global Politics Amharic Horn Geopolitics Amharic Horn Review Journal Articles Amharic horn review magazine Amharic Report News and Events Contact Us 2026-11-02 National Ownership or Premature Abandonment in Somalia’s Dangerous New Phase 0 Comments The Ugandan drawdown from Lower Shabelle, the political crisis surrounding the contested extension of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s mandate and the termination of the United Nations political mission after more than three decades of continuous presence are not discrete events. Assessed collectively they have an inflection point in Somalia’s conflict with Al Shabaab and a single interlocking configuration of retrenchment articulated through the discourse of sovereignty and national ownership. The proposition this configuration yields is both straightforward and disquieting which shows Somalia is being propelled into a higher risk phase of the war while remaining politically disintegrated and militarily incomplete and the external support system that has sustained the state is being dismantled before any credible indigenous substitute has come up. With the military dimension because it is the most immediately consequential Uganda has been the largest and longest serving contributor to the African Union mission since 2007 and its forces both under AUSSOM and through bilateral arrangements have held key positions across Lower Shabelle. The river towns and forward operating bases around Barawe, Bulo Marer, Qoryoley and Janaale constitute the main western buffer for Mogadishu. The first batch of roughly one hundred and nine troops departed and bilateral elements are exiting faster still with the full Ugandan drawdown targeted for completion by late 2027 or August 2027 in earlier statements. President Museveni explicitly rejected Mohamud’s request to delay the withdrawal. The reality is that Ugandan units have repeatedly been the difference between holding ground and losing it. The Somali National Army has a record of struggling to hold territory. Al Shabaab ran an offensive in 2025 across Middle and Lower Shabelle taking towns close to the capital before some were clawed back with Ugandan, SNA, American and Turkish support. Rural areas and many supply corridors remain under Al Shabaab influence or contested. Removing the main reliable force from the critical space raises the odds of further gains by the insurgency, more ambushes on convoys and greater pressure on Mogadishu’s perimeter. This is not an orderly and capability matched handover. It is donor and troop contributor fatigue meeting an unfinished fight. The political crisis compounds the military vulnerability and the two cannot be analysed in isolation. Mohamud’s term formally expired in mid May 2026 under the prior constitutional reading. Parliament passed amendments extending presidential and parliamentary terms to five years which his government treats as extending his mandate to May 2027. The opposition including the leaders of Puntland and Jubaland, former presidents and others rejects this as illegitimate and disputes the 2027 election timetable. There has been violence in Mogadishu over the issue earlier in and a Supreme Court challenge remains pending. Museveni reportedly pressed Mohamud on dialogue with the opposition while linking continued presence to political progress. The Russia and Africa Summit trip was cancelled amid a deadly Al-Shabaab ambush that killed dozens of SNA soldiers in Bay and the southwest plus these domestic pressures and the foreign minister led a lower level delegation instead. The reality here is that security and politics are linked. A divided federal government cannot generate coherent national forces, mobilize clans effectively against Al Shabaab or sustain pressure in the field. Foreign partners Uganda included see the political paralysis and reduce commitment. Al-Shabaab thrives on exactly this combination of governance gaps, elite squabbling and selective federal regional tensions. The withdrawal of Ugandan troops is a political signal that says the principal security guarantor has concluded that its continued presence is not justified by the political path of the recipient state. Into this void steps the termination of the United Nations political mission. UNTMIS closed on 31 October 2026 after a two year transition requested by the Somali government ending more than three decades of continuous UN political presence stretching from UNPOS through UNSOM to UNTMIS. Functions transfer to Somali institutions and to remaining UN agencies, funds and programs. The UN notes progress on institutions while underlining the Al Shabaab threat and continued support through other channels. AUSSOM is a separate military mission. This is largely optics and national ownership language. The political mission’s departure removes a layer of external mediation and coordination at the exact moment political legitimacy is contested and the military transition is incomplete. Agencies stay for aid and technical work but the dedicated political structure is gone. The mediation capacity that once convened federal and regional leaders, that monitored political agreements and that provided a neutral venue for dispute resolution has been dissolved precisely when the dispute over the electoral timetable and the legitimacy of the presidency is at its most acute. National ownership is a worthy aspiration but ownership presupposes a functioning owner. Somalia’s federal institutions remain contested, its regional states pursue divergent strategies and its parliament has become the instrument of a contested mandate extension rather than a forum for national consensus. The structural logic connecting these three developments is Uganda’s departure weakens the military buffer. The political crisis erodes the legitimacy that any military effort requires. The closure of the UN political mission removes the external mediation that might have bridged the political divide. Each development reinforces the others. A government that cannot convene its own regions cannot coordinate a national counterinsurgency. A military that cannot hold ground without foreign partners cannot fill the gap left by departing Ugandan units. Somalia is still heavily dependent on external military and logistical support against Al Shabaab that controls or influences large rural stretches of the center and south. The insurgency does not require a decisive military victory to profit from this moment. It requires only that the gaps widen, that convoys grow more vulnerable, that clan militias hedge their loyalties and that the government’s authority contract to the neighbourhoods of Mogadishu it can still control. Security and politics are linked and neither can be sequenced ahead of the other. A government that lacks legitimacy cannot mobilize the population against an embedded insurgency. An insurgency that offers governance, taxation and dispute resolution in the countryside will outcompete a distant and divided state. Somalia is being left more to its own devices before it has demonstrated the capacity to secure the territory that matters most. The language of national ownership is not false in its aspiration but it is premature in its application. The political mission’s departure, the Ugandan drawdown and the unresolved constitutional crisis together constitute that the Somali state can absorb responsibilities it has not yet shown it can discharge. The higher risk phase of the war has begun and it has begun while Somalia remains politically divided and militarily incomplete. football.content: خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق — تاق برس اعجاب المتابعين الإثنين, نوفمبر 2, 2026 من نحن السياسة التحريرية للإعلان على تاق برس اتصل بنا تاق برس - اخبار السودان والعالم الرئيسية أخبار عاجلة سياسية منوعات وثقافة إقتصاد رياضة علوم وتكنلوجيا مقالات أخري تقارير صحة الرئيسية أخبار رياضة خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق بواسطة editor في أكتوبر 31, 2026 230 مشاركة متابعات تاق برس – تتجه العلاقة بين الغاني كواسي أبياه، المدير الفني للمنتخب الوطني السوداني الأول، والاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم نحو منعطف بالغ الخطورة، في ظل تصاعد الضغوط والتدخلات التي باتت تحاصر المدرب، وتضع تجربته مع صقور الجديان على المحك، وسط مؤشرات متزايدة على اقتراب نهاية مشواره مع المنتخب. وتشير المعلومات التي تحصل عليها “الترا سودان” من داخل مجلس إدارة الاتحاد إلى أن أبياه بات يشعر بأن ما يتعرض له يمثل تحركات منظمة تستهدف تقويض صلاحياته وإضعاف موقفه، تمهيداً لإبعاده عن قيادة المنتخب. وهو ما أسرّ به لعدد من المقربين منه، معبّراً عن استيائه الشديد من الأجواء التي يعمل فيها. وبحسب المعلومات ذاتها، فإن المدرب الغاني بات يعتقد أن هناك مخططاً يُحاك ضده، وأن بعض القرارات والتوجهات الأخيرة داخل الاتحاد لا يمكن فصلها عن مساعٍ لإجباره على مغادرة موقعه، بعدما وجد نفسه في مواجهة تدخلات متكررة في صميم اختصاصاته الفنية. التغييرات التي طالت الجهازين الإداري والفني المساعد لم تكن أمراً عابراً بالنسبة للمدرب الغاني، خصوصاً بعد إبعاد المدير الإداري أبوبكر الماحي، وابتعاد المدرب العام صلاح الفنج عن موقعه ضمن المنظومة التي عملت معه خلال الفترة الماضية. ويمثل الرجلان عنصرين مهمين في منظومة أبياه، وكان المدرب ينظر إليهما باعتبارهما من ركائز الاستقرار داخل المنتخب، الأمر الذي دفعه إلى المطالبة بإعادة ترتيب الأوضاع بما يضمن عودة الانسجام إلى الجهازين الفني والإداري. لكن ما حدث عزز شعوره بأن هناك توجهاً لإعادة تشكيل المنظومة المحيطة به، دون اعتبار لرؤيته أو احتياجاته، وبكوادر لا تمتلك بالضرورة الخبرة المطلوبة للعمل في منتخب بحجم صقور الجديان. ومن أكثر الملفات التي أثارت غضب أبياه الضغوط المتواصلة بشأن إبعاد عدد من أصحاب الخبرة والعناصر الأساسية التي شكلت العمود الفقري للمنتخب خلال مشواره الأخير. فالمدرب الغاني لا يرى مبرراً للتخلي عن عناصر أثبتت جدارتها وقدمت التوجه نحو تغيير نسبة من قوام المنتخب وإقحام عناصر من منتخب الشباب، في وقت يرى فيه أبياه أن الإحلال والتجديد لا ينبغي أن يتحولا إلى قرارات فوقية تتجاوز التقييم الفني واحتياجات المنتخب. ولم تتوقف مصادر
